item.title: ‘The Snackbar at the End of the World’ releases trailer and Steam page
item.category: The Snackbar at the End of the World
item.description:
The Snackbar at the End of the World is a narrative driven adventure RPG where you are not only becoming a chef and cooking your way back to success in your family’s restaurant, but you also need to fight off vegetables that have grown with human characteristics and do not want to be harvested in the magical area beyond the city’s walls.

As you look to collect ingredients, you will need to fight your way through strange enemies, who look a lot like the food you are after. If killing them is a bit much, there are several changes to sneak past them, in hopes that you can harvest what isn’t currently walking around. Then, you will need to take your harvest and cook it up – using little mini-game-esque …

item.title: ‘Power Line’ shows you that you’ve lied on your resume, to work for Nintendo
item.description:
Power Line is a narrative driven game that is inspired by the real Nintendo Power Line game call center, where players were able to call a physical phoneline and get hints when they were stuck in Nintendo games. It’s an interesting job, and one that no longer is a thing due to the nature of the internet, but back in the 1980s was in demand.

In Power Line your job is to answer the phone and help people out with a fictional game, one that you have never played both in the game and in real life. You have applied and got the job despite having lied on your resume. They feel that you are perfect for the job, so must answer the phone and be able to decide what …

item.title: Help rebuild a town hit by meteors in ‘Moonfrost’
item.description:
Moonfrost is a cozy, farming-style game where you are a Frost Hunter, who has come to a new town in hopes of making the town a better place. However, you have not remembered anything before today and now need to start from scratch, fixing up the town and building up your own home.

Moonfrost has a lot of the key things that farming games have; the ability to create a bunch of different tools, lots of foraging, a small town full of people that want to talk to you. You can spend your days growing crops, selling them to Frost Hunter boards, and helping gather the resources needed to revived the town. item.title: ‘Did a Monkey Write This?’ has you outsourcing book writing to AI
item.description:
In the era of 2026, more and more creative industries are being, confusingly, outsource to AI; creative writing, publishing games and more. In Did a Monkey Write This? you are a young author, who has hit writers block and finds writing books too overwhelming – after all, on Amazon, there are thousands of books published each day – how are you meant to compete? Thankfully, you have your own pet ape that is able to write the rest of your book for you. This ape also had the idea to hire their cousins, also known as Ape Intelligence or AI, to write the rest of your books and make millions.

item.title: Solve Puzzles and Find Shinies in ‘Bad Magpie’
item.description:
In Bad Magpie, you play as a little magpie that has wounded their wings. Now that the world has given you a bad time, you will be fighting back by setting things on fire, smashing places up and taking what you want most; something shiny!

You can find different shiny objects throughout each of the levels, which you then trade in for trinkets that your magpie especially wants. The world feels quite big, but at the same time, you are sort of led around through chasing the shiny objects and various puzzles that present themselves. Sometimes these puzzles have you striking rocks to set things on fire or getting your head stuck in walls, then tearing them down.

Your end goal in Bad Magpie is actually to cure your own …

item.title: Every animal has its place in ‘Tidy Up the Ark’
item.description:
I swear, when I heard of Noah’s Ark, it was two of each animal. Not 20! But I guess higher numbers have never been an issue. So, in Tidy up the Ark, you are meant to get all of the different animals to their specific pens, so that they are ready for the great flood. It’s a simple game, one of those sort of cozy, clean-up style things, where you can watch the world transform as you clean up areas and put everything in the right spot.

The game itself is simple, almost mindless. There is a massive ark, with three floors. One houses the herbivores, one the omnivores and one the carnivores. Luckily for you, most of the animals on the floor you find them on are in the …

item.title: ‘Showrunners’ has you roller skating around massive courses!
item.description:
Showrunners is a fast paced, speed-running roller skating game where you are trying to build up high speed, land tricks, and master your movement so that you can come out on the top of the leader board. The story behind this game has you racing for entertainment, of those watching your performance. You can change out your outfits and do various tricks to better entertain the crowd.

The movement in Showrunners feels really good – going from a pipe to a road to a side wall all starts to flow and feel good. With that said, sometimes it’s not quite straight forward where you are going, and you might need to die a few times and respawn to actually understand the way of each of the tracks. Once you do …

item.title: Build your own world in ‘Fangtopia’
item.description:
Fangtopia is a relaxing, spooky-themed puzzle game where you are creating a world for ghosts, monsters and ghouls through placing a bunch of hexagon tiles onto a map. You can build on what is already there, adding trees to forests and houses to towns, which combo them up to increase your points. You can also get some special tiles over time, which are through two choices, that need completing within your town.

Fangtopia has a few different game modes, from a short game mode that has bite-sized sessions to a large island building mode for longer sessions. There is also an Island Mode where you can connect a bunch of different archipelagos by putting down ghost train tracks! It’s quite interesting watching the world itself grow and come to life …

item.title: Roll dice and make it big in ‘Influencer Solitaire’
item.description:
If only becoming an influencer was as easy rolling some dice and placing them on cards! That’s exactly what you can do in Influencer Solitaire, a game all about rolling dice, setting up your campaigns, and seeing if you can make the audience you need.

Each day, you will wake up with some dice to roll. You can then spend them on your life – a job to pay your rent, research to better understand video content (through unlocking cards) and other every-day activities. You can also spend them on your hobby; becoming a massive influencer. Some cards need specific dice, some give better results when you have higher dice, and others just need a die so that they will activate.

item.title: ‘Future? No Thanks!’ hilariously rejects future tech
item.description:
Future? No Thanks! is a hilarious story-driven open world adventure game where you have aged, to an old, maybe slightly sexist man who is surrounded by the advancements of society. And instead of embracing the future, you have decided it’s best for you just to die. As a result, it is your last day on Earth, but the doctors who will be performing your end of life care want you to go out into the world and do a few tasks to make sure you have done everything you could possibly want to do before you die.

Some of these tasks, which you have defined, are things like ‘get into a fight’ which is absolutely wild for an elder grandfather to be doing. You do have a strange robot dog …
